There are no slides, jumps or water sports; the 'action' is the party energy, placed early (6–9s) and mid (18–21s) to break up static venue shots.
study.views: The biggest view comes early, at 4.33–5.96s (1.63s). It is a gimbal pan across the lagoon-style pool, revealing turquoise water, tall palms, a row of palapa umbrellas and white clouds; it is the fastest smooth move in the video (motion 47–54). It is introduced by the walk-up at 3.13–4.33s, where the palm path frames the 'HIBISCUS' sign in the distance (a walk-toward reveal). The other wides are: the opening lobby (0–3.13s, the longest hold at 3.13s, slow push-in, symmetrical); La Casita's piñata dome (16.47–18.62s, 2.15s, slow lateral glide); the pink shopping street under clear blue sky (23.4–25.1s, 1.7s, slow pan); and the closing bar (29.73–33.38s, 3.64s, slow push-in). There is no drone, no ocean, no sunset and no room view. The 'wow' is architecture and color, not scenery.
study.how_place_is_shown: Mostly gimbal-stabilized, eye-level-to-low wides and mediums of empty or lightly occupied spaces, filmed as an unseen visitor (POV walk-throughs, no presenter). People appear only in the party and show shots (crowds of adult guests, performers) and as incidental staff (spa therapist, bartenders), which reinforces 'adults-only' without casting anyone. The light mix: bright midday sun with blue sky outdoors (pool, shops); warm, moody low light for indoor dining (9.4–12.47s); saturated colored stage light for the night show. The details are signage, not food: the venue signs themselves (Cozumel neon, The Smoked neon sculpture, Le Gourmet painted plaque, Mikado calligraphy, shop signs) act as visual name tags, so viewers can match the name to the place. No dishes or drinks are shown, though the closing neon 'ALL YOU NEED IS TEQUILA' doubles as a drink cue.
study.info_and_value: All information is in on-screen text; there is no voiceover. Facts given: adults-only, all-inclusive, modern-meets-Mexican design. Named venues: Hibiscus Pool (laid-back), Tequila Pool Bar (party), Cozumel Buffet (breakfast, lunch and dinner), The Smoked Restaurant (Texas-inspired slow-cooked steakhouse), Le Gourmet (classic French), Mikado (Japanese), La Casita (Mexican by day, show stage by night), Bahia Spa (world-class), on-site shops with locally-made goods, and a centrally-located pharmacy. There are no prices, booking dates or resort name. The value is the 'here's everything inside' checklist: 2 pool vibes, 5 named restaurants, spa, shops and pharmacy. That reassures first-timers that they never need to leave the property, which makes the video worth saving and sending to a travel partner. The booking path is the CTA 'CONTACT YOUR TRAVEL AGENT!'
study.pacing: 20 shots in 33.4s (5.69 cuts per 10s). Median shot 1.54s, shortest 1.03s, longest 3.64s (ending). The structure has 3 speeds. The opening hook is held 3.13s. The middle is a steady run of 1.1–1.8s shots, with the restaurant list cut almost metronomically: 1.27s / 1.27s / 1.27s for Cozumel, Smoked and Le Gourmet, then 1.47s and 2.16s. The ending is held 3.64s for the CTA. Each named venue gets exactly one shot, except the pool (2), the party (2), the night show (2) and the shops (4 shots under one caption). Cuts lock to the music closely in the first half: 3.13 vs a hit at 3.19, 5.96 vs 5.84, 7.73 vs 7.85, 9.4 vs 9.47, 12.47 vs 12.52 and 18.62 vs 18.51 (all within ~0.12s). In the second half the cuts drift off the beat. Motion is high (35–56) through the pool and party section (3–10s), mid through dining, and calms to 10–23 from 26s on, so the video winds down into the CTA.
study.speed: none — everything appears to play at normal speed. The slow feel of the lobby (0–3s) and bar (29.7–33.4s) comes from slow gimbal push-ins, not slow motion.
study.on_screen_text: One caption block per section, sitting in the lower-middle third (~62–78% down the frame), centered or left-aligned, over the footage with no box. Each block is 1–2 lines: a small white sans lead-in plus a large script-font name, with a soft shadow. Blocks: 0–3.13 'Check out this adults-only all-inclusive resort with a' (sans) + 'modern-meets-Mexican vibe!' (script). 3.13–5.96 'Relax at the laid-back' + 'Hibiscus Pool'. 5.96–9.4 'or party it up at the' + 'Tequila Pool Bar!', switched to royal blue to match the party energy. 9.4–11.2 'Savor the flavor at the many dining venues available, such as...' (sans only, 2 lines). Restaurants 11.2–18.62: script name + white sans one-liner, e.g. 'Cozumel Buffet / Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner', 'The Smoked Restaurant / Texas-inspired slow-cooked steakhouse', 'Le Gourmet / Sophisticated classic French dining', 'Mikado / A traditional Japanese-style favorite', 'La Casita / Serving Mexican flavors during the day'. 18.62–21.33 'then transforming into a stage for vibrant shows at night!' (sans, 2 lines). 21.33–23.4 'Treat yourself at the world-class' + 'Bahia Spa'. 23.4–25.1 'There's also a variety of shops on the property'. 25.1–28.37 'where you can shop for locally-made goods' (one caption held across 3 shots). 28.37–29.73 'and a centrally-located pharmacy!'. 29.73–~31.3 'READY FOR AN ADULTS-ONLY GETAWAY?' then ~31.3–33.38 'CONTACT YOUR TRAVEL AGENT!' in a large white hand-drawn marker-style all-caps font, centered mid-frame. Captions change exactly on the cuts. They read as one running sentence across shots ('...such as...', 'then transforming...', 'where you can...', 'and a...'), which pulls the viewer forward. No emoji. Lead-ins run ~4–12 words; names run 1–3 words.
study.audio: A licensed music track with no voiceover. The only detected words, 'Thank you' at 0.50–1.20s, are a vocal sample in the music, not narration. There is no natural sound of splashes or crowds. Strong hits at 0.19, 3.19, 5.84/6.12, 7.85, 9.47, 12.52 and 18.51/18.79 line up with cuts. The underwater-to-foam-party drop (5.96) and the day-to-night La Casita switch (18.62) are the two moments placed on the clearest hits.
study.transitions: Mostly hard cuts on the beat. One water-dip transition at 5.96s: the frame after the cut is underwater (bubbles, pool tiles) and the shot rises up through the surface into the foam party, so the 'relax' pool and the 'party' pool are joined by going underwater. Around 7.3–7.7s the party frames and caption look ghosted or motion-blurred, which reads as a blur/shake effect going into the 7.73 cut. The La Casita day-to-night switch at 18.62 is a match on location (same piñata dome, same angle family) using a hard cut. The text swap at ~31.3s inside the final shot acts as an in-shot transition from question to CTA.
study.effects: Slow digital or gimbal push-ins on the hook (0–3.13s) and the end (29.73–33.38s). There is a mild bright, saturated grade: boosted turquoise in the pool and party water, strong reds in the Cozumel and Le Gourmet shots, saturated pinks and greens in the village. Natural sun flare and light leak sit on The Diamond storefront (25.1–26.2s). There is possible motion blur or a ghosting effect on the party shot around 7.3–7.7s. Text color changes once (blue for the Tequila Pool Bar). No maps, split screens or freeze frames.
study.quality: 1080x1920 at 24fps, H.264 at ~15.2 Mbps, so it is sharp with little compression. The look is gimbal-smooth throughout; median motion is 24.7 and comes from deliberate moves, not shake. Exposure is bright, with some blown-out skies in the shop and pool shots (white clouds, sun flare), and the night dining shots are slightly noisy. The party shots use an ultra-wide action-cam look with distortion and droplets, which feels fun and immersive. Overall it reads as polished agent or brand footage: clean, colorful and dreamy enough. It doesn't feel like a phone snapshot because of the stabilization, the steady pacing and the consistent typography system.
study.ending: It ends on the most stylish interior: the bar with the neon 'ALL YOU NEED IS TEQUILA' sign, held 3.64s (the longest shot) with a slow push-in. A two-step text close runs first as a question ('READY FOR AN ADULTS-ONLY GETAWAY?', ~1.6s), then as a direct CTA ('CONTACT YOUR TRAVEL AGENT!', ~2.1s), which stays on screen to the last frame. There is no designed loop, though the calm interior fits loosely with the calm lobby opener.
study.why_viral: 1) The hook is a strange, gorgeous visual: a giant neon alebrije cat under a palapa roof. The two qualifiers that self-select the audience, 'adults-only' and 'all-inclusive', sit in the first line, so the right viewers instantly feel 'this is for me'. 2) It contrasts 'relax' with 'party': a calm lagoon pool, then a water-dip transition into a foam party, followed later by La Casita going from piñata-filled lunch spot to fire-baton show at night. That shows the resort has multiple moods. 3) It is a fast, readable inventory (2 pools, 5 named restaurants each with a one-line cuisine tag, spa, shops, pharmacy). That answers the 'is there enough to do and eat?' question that makes people save and send to a partner. 4) The color-saturated, beat-cut, gimbal footage paired with an elegant two-font caption system feels premium in 33s.
lessons: Open on the single most unusual visual on the property (a statue, sign or architecture) held ~3s with a slow push-in. Put the audience qualifiers ('adults-only', 'all-inclusive', 'family') in the very first text line.
Use a two-tier caption system: a small sans lead-in sentence plus a big script venue name, in the lower-middle third (~65–75% down), changed exactly on the cut. Keep each lead-in to 4–12 words.
Write the captions as one running sentence across shots ('...such as...', 'then...', 'where you can...', 'and a...'). This makes viewers keep watching to finish the thought.

For lists of venues, give each item one 1.2–1.5s shot of its sign or entrance plus a 4–6 word descriptor (cuisine, hours), at near-identical shot lengths. In this video 3 restaurants in a row are each 1.27s.

Build a calm-versus-energy contrast early: show the relaxing version (pool pan) for ~3s, then hit the beat into the party version by ~6s. Join them with a water dip, a whip or another motivated transition.
Look for one day-to-night or before-after twist at the same location (La Casita by day, then a show at night). Cut it on a strong audio hit and keep the angle similar so the change reads instantly.
Snap cuts to the music's strong hits within ~0.1s in the first half, where retention matters most. Let the second half breathe and slow motion down (to ~10–20) heading into the CTA.

End on the most atmospheric interior held 3.5s+ with a slow push-in. Use a two-step text close (aspirational question ~1.5s, then the booking action ~2s), and keep the final CTA on screen through the last frame.

When there are no prices, add utility facts that answer practical worries (pharmacy on site, buffet hours, shops). Those are the details that make people save the video and forward it to a travel partner.

name: FULL - Camp Ocean Carnival Mardi Gras.MOV

study.format: Kids-club amenity tour: a silent, text-led walkthrough of one ship venue. There are 12 handheld walking shots. Each info card stays up across 1 to 3 shots and works like a mini fact sheet: what it is, who it's for, age groups, activities, the bonus area, then a wrap-up line. The middle section is a list that builds on screen (three age groups) as the camera moves through the rooms. There is no voiceover and no presenter.
study.place: Camp Ocean, the kids club on the Carnival Mardi Gras cruise ship, plus the Dr. Seuss Bookville library. It opens on the ship docked at a pier under a clear blue sky. Inside are ocean-themed rooms with fish and penguin murals, glowing fish-shaped crawl tunnels in yellow, orange and purple, gaming pods with TVs and stools, and a check-in desk dressed for Halloween with bats, pumpkins and ghosts. Bookville has neon Dr. Seuss signage, Thing 1/Thing 2, Sam-I-Am and Grinch murals, lit bookshelves and a yellow hand-shaped bench. It is a family cruise, and the appeal is that kids get their own themed world on board.
study.audience: Parents, and grandparents, thinking about a Carnival cruise with kids aged 2 to 11 or 12, who want to know if the kids will be entertained and safe. It makes them want to save it for planning, send it to a partner or co-parent, and feel the cruise is kid-proof. It reads as a family-cruise creator or travel agent doing a factual venue preview: informative and brand-friendly, not the cruise line's own polished ad and not a personal vlog (no faces, no talking).
study.hook: Frame 1 is the huge Carnival Mardi Gras hull and superstructure filling the right two-thirds of the frame against a deep blue sky, filmed walking along a pier railing over the water. A three-line title sits dead center from 0.0s: 'TAKE A PEEK INSIDE' / 'Camp Ocean' (large, rounded, light-blue bold letters) / 'ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS'. Music starts on an audio hit at 0.04s. It stops the scroll because the instantly recognizable giant ship works as an establishing view, and 'take a peek inside' promises access to a members-only space (the kids club) that parents can't usually see before booking. The named ship and venue also tell searchers right away that this is exactly what they're looking for.

beats.what: Ship exterior from the pier, handheld walk along the railing, with the title 'TAKE A PEEK INSIDE Camp Ocean ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS'.
Camp Ocean check-in desk with glowing logo and Halloween decorations. The title carries over and the camera pushes toward the desk and a 'TURTLES' age-group sign.
Walk through a room with fish and crab murals, a TV and cubbies. Text: 'KIDS AGES 2-11 CAN EXPERIENCE A FUN SUMMER CAMP ALL ABOARD THEIR CARNIVAL CRUISE!'
Close-up of glowing fish-shaped crawl tunnels (yellow, then orange, then purple). Text: 'CAMPERS ARE SPLIT AMONGST AGE-BASED GROUPS:'
'🐧 PENGUINS: AGE 2-5' added under the header, mid-shot.
Cut to the penguin and orca mural room with soft chairs. '🌊 STINGRAYS: AGE 6-8' appears on the cut, with a fast pan (peak motion 75 at 10.5s).
'🦈 SHARKS: AGE 9-12' added as the camera pans to the play kitchens and workbench.
Activity room with round stools and wall TVs in arched pods. Text lists activities: arts and crafts, songs, games, toys, dancing, movies and video games.
Closer handheld drift around the gaming pods and TVs; the same text holds until 18.53.
Cat in the Hat cutout with a Halloween ghost, then a slow pan across the glowing neon 'Dr. Seuss Bookville' sign (motion drops to 8-14). Text: 'AND DON'T FORGET THE DR. SUESS BOOKVILLE™'.
The pan comes off the sign onto the glass entrance, revealing the colorful library inside.
Wide of the Bookville interior with red/white ceiling stripes, Seuss murals and wave seating. Text: 'IMAGINE A NORMAL LIBRARY PUT THROUGH THE WORLD OF DR.SEUSS!'
Walk past the Thing 1/Thing 2 mural to lit bookshelves, then a Sam-I-Am close-up. The text clears around 27.3, leaving clean art.
Whimsical colorful armchair and yellow hand-shaped bench, slow handheld push along the bench. No text.
Lit bookshelf wall ('Take a look at a book / and when you're done / return the fun!') next to the Grinch mural. Closing text: 'THERE'S FUN FOR ALL CHILDREN ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS!'

study.action_shots: No people doing activities. The only motion is the camera walking through spaces. The pier walk runs 0-2.53s (follow-style forward walk, normal speed). The fastest move is a whip-like pan through the penguin room at 10.37-13s (motion 50-75, the highest in the video), which lands right as the 'STINGRAYS' line appears, with the cut at 10.37 about 0.13s after the 10.24 audio hit. The Bookville walk-through from 25.13-30.07 (motion 31-45) moves past murals and shelves. All footage plays at real speed.
study.views: Only one true scenic view: the ship exterior at 0-2.53s. The camera is handheld, walking along the pier railing so the hull slides and grows in frame, with blue sky and water. It is held for the full 2.53s and is the biggest visual in the video. It is used up front as the hook, not saved for later. Inside, the 'view reveal' is the Bookville sequence: an almost still pan across the neon sign (20-22.5s, motion 8-14) that slides off the sign onto the glass doors at about 22.4s. A hard cut at 23.47 then lands the room wide. No drone, no balcony, no sunsets.
study.how_place_is_shown: Almost entirely POV handheld phone walking, at chest height, with no people. There are no kids (privacy, and the club was likely empty at embarkation or during an open house). A stranger's arm and hand appear only briefly at 15.1s. The mix is about 40% medium room walk-throughs, 35% details (fish tunnels, TVs, murals, bookshelves, chairs) and a few wides (pier, Bookville entrance and interior). Light is bright midday outside, then cool fluorescent and LED blue-purple inside, with warm accents from the backlit tunnels and yellow shelves. Details are chosen to show kid-pleasing design: themed crawl holes, play kitchens, gaming pods, character art, so parents imagine their kids in the space.
study.info_and_value: All information is on-screen text with no voiceover: ship name (Carnival Mardi Gras), venue name (Camp Ocean), ages 2-11, and that it works like a 'summer camp'. Age groups: Penguins 2-5, Stingrays 6-8, Sharks 9-12 (note this conflicts with the earlier 2-11 claim). Activities listed: arts and crafts, songs, games, toys, dancing, movies, video games. There is a bonus venue (Dr. Seuss Bookville, misspelled 'SUESS' in one card) and a wrap-up line 'There's fun for all children'. No prices, hours or booking info. The age-group list is the most saveable part: a quick reference that parents screenshot or send to a partner.
study.pacing: 12 shots in 35.3s, 3.12 cuts per 10s, median shot 2.82s, range 1.6-4.93s. Each text card gets roughly 2.5-4.9s of reading time and stays on screen across cuts: the title spans 2 shots (4.53s), the age list spans 2 shots (6.47s), activities span 2 shots (4.46s), and Bookville gets one long 4.93s shot. The music hits roughly every 1.8s (1.84, 10.24, 12.04, 13.84, 15.64, ... 33.64). Three cuts land on or near a hit: 10.37 (+0.13), 15.67 (+0.03), 30.07 (+0.03). Most other cuts are placed for reading time, not for the beat. The rhythm is a steady, calm stroll, with a busier middle (10-13s, motion up to 75) and a slow, still moment on the neon sign (20-22.5s, motion 8-14). The final three shots run without text or with short text, giving a relaxed outro.
study.on_screen_text: Everything is centered on screen. The body text is a white condensed bold sans (Bebas/Oswald-style) in all caps with a soft dark drop shadow and no box. The title uses a mixed treatment: two lines of white condensed caps sandwich 'Camp Ocean' in a much larger rounded heavy font, light blue with a white outline. Cards: 0-4.53 title (9 words); 4.53-7.6 'KIDS AGES 2-11 CAN EXPERIENCE A FUN SUMMER CAMP ALL ABOARD THEIR CARNIVAL CRUISE!' (3 lines); 7.6-14.07 header 'CAMPERS ARE SPLIT AMONGST AGE-BASED GROUPS:' sits at the upper third while the list builds line by line below it: '🐧 PENGUINS: AGE 2-5' (about 9.2s), '🌊 STINGRAYS: AGE 6-8' (10.37), '🦈 SHARKS: AGE 9-12' (about 12.1). 14.07-18.53: a 4-line activities list (about 22 words, the densest card). 18.53-23.47: 'AND DON'T FORGET THE DR. SUESS BOOKVILLE™'. 23.47 to about 27.3: 'IMAGINE A NORMAL LIBRARY PUT THROUGH THE WORLD OF DR.SEUSS!' 27.3-33.13: no text. 33.13-35.3: 'THERE'S FUN FOR ALL CHILDREN ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS!' Emoji are used only as bullet icons for the age groups. Text pops on and off with no animation.
study.audio: Music only, with no speech and no audible natural sound. It is an upbeat track with strong hits about every 1.8s, starting at 0.04s. Picture and sound line up loosely: the Stingrays reveal and fast pan (10.37), the activities pod cut (15.67) and the cut to the colorful chairs (30.07) land within 0.13s of hits. The rest of the cuts follow the text timing rather than the music.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only (2.53, 4.53, 7.6, 10.37, 14.07, 15.67, 18.53, 23.47, 25.13, 30.07, 33.13). The pan from the neon sign to the glass doors at about 22.4s acts as an in-camera reveal before the 23.47 cut.
study.effects: No zooms, freeze frames, graphics, maps or split screens. Color is close to straight off the phone. The exterior is naturally saturated blue. Interiors lean cool blue and purple from the venue lighting, with slight bloom and glow on the backlit fish tunnels and neon sign. Any grade is minimal.
study.quality: 1080x1920, 30fps, HEVC at about 12.7 Mbps, so it looks sharp on stills and murals. Handheld phone stabilization is decent but floaty, and the fast pans at 10-13s and some walking moments show motion blur and mild judder. The exterior is well exposed with a deep blue sky. Interiors are a little flat and cool under fluorescent light, with some soft focus on close-ups (tunnels at 8.5s, Sam-I-Am at 27.5s). It reads as an honest phone walkthrough, not a dream-trip cinematic piece. That fits the 'real preview for parents' intent and builds trust.
study.ending: Ends on a bright, color-packed bookshelf wall with the Grinch mural and the wrap-up line 'THERE'S FUN FOR ALL CHILDREN ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS!' (33.13-35.3, 2.17s), with a final audio hit at 34.84 just before the end. There is no explicit save, follow or book CTA. The summary line does that job emotionally. It doesn't loop seamlessly (the bookshelf doesn't match the opening ship shot), but its short length makes rewatching easy.
study.why_viral: 1) It answers a high-anxiety, searchable question for parents ('what's the kids club like on Mardi Gras?') with real footage of a space you normally only see after boarding. 2) The age-group list (Penguins, Stingrays, Sharks) builds on screen, giving instantly useful, screenshot-worthy info, and it's the kind of detail parents send to a partner. 3) Big licensed IP (Dr. Seuss Bookville, Cat in the Hat, Grinch) plus Halloween décor makes the rooms look magical and gives a 'bonus' payoff in the second half. 4) The recognizable giant ship in frame 1 plus 'take a peek inside' sets up curiosity and access within 2 seconds.
lessons: Open on the most recognizable exterior (ship, hotel facade, park gate) for 2-2.5s, with a 3-line centered title: small verb line / big branded name in a contrasting rounded colored font / small location line.
For amenity tours, keep one text card on screen across 2 shots (about 4-6.5s total) so viewers can read while the footage changes underneath. Change text on cuts, not mid-sentence.
Turn facts into a list that builds on screen: add one line every 1.5-3s (here about 9.2, 10.37, 12.1s), ideally timed to a cut or a music hit, with an emoji bullet per item.
Use white condensed all-caps text with a soft drop shadow, centered, max about 4 lines. Push the densest card to about 20 words only if it's held 4s or more.
Put your fastest pan right where a new list item appears (here motion peaked at 75 at the 10.37 Stingrays reveal) so information and energy land together.
Save a bonus area for the back half ('and don't forget...') and reveal it with a slow, near-still pan (motion under 15) across signage that slides onto the entrance, then hard cut to the wide.
Leave 4-6s near the end with no text over the most colorful details so the place can breathe, then close on one summary line over the brightest wide.
Don't show other people's kids. Empty, well-lit rooms with props (tunnels, play kitchens, TVs) let parents picture their own children and avoid privacy issues.
Snap at least the key cuts to music hits (within 0.1s here at 15.67 and 30.07). When text needs reading time, let readability win over beat-matching.
Proofread names and numbers: 'SUESS' and the 2-11 vs 9-12 conflict here invite correction comments. Fine for engagement, but bad for an agent's credibility.

name: FULL - Choose Your Carnival Mardi Gras Vibe.MOV

study.format: 'Choose your vibe' guide that works as a zone-by-zone ship tour. A water-level hook shot of the ship carries the question. Then four named ship zones follow, each built the same way: a signage shot that acts as the title card, followed by 1-3 'what you get' shots, each with its own benefit subtitle. Most chapters run 3-4 shots and about 10-11s. There is no voiceover, no numbering and no explicit 'comment your pick' line; the zone names are the options.
study.place: Carnival Mardi Gras cruise ship, shown docked in turquoise Caribbean water. The four on-board zones are: Loft 19 (paid adults' retreat with private cabanas, an infinity whirlpool and ocean-front loungers), BOLT (the first rollercoaster at sea, plus mini golf under the track at sunset), Serenity (adults-only deck with a bar and a pool with a lit blue waterfall wall) and Grand Central (theater with Vegas-style live shows). What makes it special is that a ship holds a rollercoaster, private cabanas and a Vegas stage, mostly with open ocean behind them.
study.audience: People who have booked or are considering a Mardi Gras or Carnival cruise: couples wanting adult-only space, parents ('take some time away from the kids') and thrill-seekers (BOLT). It invites them to comment which vibe they'd pick, tag their cruise partner and save it as a ship guide before sailing. It reads as a cruise creator or travel agent (phone footage, informational subtitles), not as Carnival's own polished brand content.
study.hook: Frame 1 is a low, water-level shot from the surface of turquoise Caribbean water. The huge Mardi Gras sits across the middle third under dramatic white clouds and blue sky, and the camera drifts slowly left. Text sits centered across the ship's hull: small 'CHOOSE YOUR VIBE ON THE', with larger 'CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS' below. There is music only and no speech; the first strong beats land at 0.65, 0.91 and 1.17s. It stops the scroll for three reasons: the swimmer's-eye angle on a giant ship is unusual, the teal water and sky are instantly 'vacation', and 'choose your vibe' promises a personal decision that makes you watch every option.

beats.what: Water-level shot of the docked Mardi Gras in turquoise water with the 'CHOOSE YOUR VIBE ON THE CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS' title (2.47s).
Option 1 title card: slow pan across the 'LOFT 19' wall letters with a warm sconce; text 'LOFT 19 / RETREAT AT SEA' (2.4s, near-static, motion 4.5-5.6).
Walk past the wooden-slat cabana with orange pillows that opens onto turf, loungers and the ocean; text 'GET YOUR OWN PRIVATE CABANA' (3.0s).
0.5s flash of the blue infinity whirlpool, then a 1.56s shot through glass doors of the same pool; text 'VISIT THE INFINITY WHIRLPOOL'.
Past a slat screen to a white lounger with a blue towel roll facing open sea, panning across the loungers; text 'RELAX ALONGSIDE THE WAVES' (3.0s).
Option 2 title card: the 'BOLT Ultimate Sea Coaster' sign and track against a sunset sky, tilting down to the deck; text 'BOLT / ROLLERCOASTER AT SEA' (3.47s).
Display coaster car with a Carnival backdrop; text 'CONTROL HOW FAST YOUR RIDE GOES' (1.73s), then a 3.1s close handheld move over the car's seats and handlebars.
Mini golf under the coaster track at pink-purple sunset with the ocean behind; text 'GET SOME 360° OCEAN VIEWS' (3.17s).
Option 3 title card: mirrored oval 'SERENITY Adult Only Retreat' sign reflecting the ship's red funnel; text 'SERENITY / ADULT ONLY RETREAT' (1.93s).
Teal daybeds in a row facing the sea; text 'TAKE SOME TIME AWAY FROM THE KIDS' (2.47s).
Sunken lounge seating with a chevron floor beside the pool; text 'ENJOY A PRIVATE BAR' (2.57s).
Pan from the lit blue waterfall wall across the pool to the sunset deck; text 'OR RELAX BY THE POOL!' (3.5s, highest motion of the video).
Option 4 title card: static shot of the Grand Central stage with the 'VEGAS NIGHTS' sign and starburst lighting; text 'GRAND CENTRAL / ENJOY A SHOW ON THE SHIP!' (3.07s).
Live performance with a singer and band under purple and pink stage lights; text 'FROM MAGIC TO MUSIC TO DANCING' (3.54s, ends the video).

study.choice_format: Question: 'Choose your vibe on the Carnival Mardi Gras', shown on the hook shot only. There are 4 options, labelled by venue name rather than numbers or emoji: LOFT 19, BOLT, SERENITY, GRAND CENTRAL. Each option shows a big bold white uppercase title in the upper third (about 23% down) with a smaller white uppercase subtitle underneath. The title stays on for the whole chapter while the subtitle changes with each shot to give a new benefit. Time and shots per option: Loft 19 runs 2.47-12.93s (10.46s, 4 shots); BOLT runs 12.93-24.4s (11.47s, 4 shots); Serenity runs 24.4-34.87s (10.47s, 4 shots); Grand Central runs 34.87-41.47s (6.6s, 2 shots). Options are separated only by a hard cut to the venue's own signage, which works as a built-in chapter card; there is no sound effect or transition. Order is quiet retreat, then thrill, then adults-only calm, then the high-energy show last. The showiest, most colorful and people-filled venue closes the video. The viewer is never told how to answer; the 'choose' framing alone implies 'comment your vibe'.
study.action_shots: There are no slides, jumps, splashes or rides; BOLT is shown only as a sign and a parked display car, not ridden. The motion is camera movement. The cabana walk-through runs 4.87-7.87s, filmed POV and handheld, with motion rising to 36 around 6.5s. The BOLT car close-ups at 18.13-21.23s are a handheld orbit (motion 24-37) running into the mini-golf move (40-44 at 21-21.5s). The fastest shot is the pool waterfall pan at 31.37-34.87s (44-48 at 31.5-32s), with falling water as the only real action. The live show at 37.93-41.47s is a static wide with the performer moving on stage (motion 2.5-4.6). Everything plays at normal speed, and cuts are not locked to the music. The 0.52s beat grid (hits at 9.18, 9.7, 10.22...) only loosely lines up with cuts; the cut at 28.8 does land on the hit at 28.84.
study.views: 0-2.47s: the ship from water level, a slow drift left with the clouds dominant. 4.87-7.87s: a walk-past reveal where wooden slats open to turf, loungers and ocean, the view arriving around 7s. 9.93-12.93s: a slat screen gives way to the open sea behind the loungers, held about 3s with a gentle pan (motion 8.6-14, the calmest moving view). 12.93-16.4s: the sunset sky behind the BOLT track, tilting down to the deck and horizon. 21.23-24.4s: the biggest and prettiest view, a pink-purple sunset over the sea framed by the coaster track, revealed by a forward glide. 26.33-28.8s: daybeds facing open sea, a slow pan. 31.37-34.87s: a pan from the waterfall wall to a dusky sea deck. The biggest view lands in the middle (about 21-24s), not at the end; the ending trades ocean for stage lights.
study.how_place_is_shown: Mostly mediums and slow-moving wides, with each chapter opened by a detail of signage (Loft letters, BOLT logo, Serenity mirror sign, Vegas Nights sign). The decks are empty: no people appear until the final show shot, which makes the retreats feel private and exclusive. Everything is filmed POV-style, handheld or phone-gimbal smooth, with no drone. Light ranges from bright midday (hook) through overcast daylight (Loft 19, Serenity) and pink golden-hour sunset (BOLT), to neon stage lighting at night (Grand Central), so the edit also reads as a day-to-night arc. Detail picks sell comfort and status: orange cushions, rolled blue towels, a chevron bar floor, the lit waterfall wall, the coaster's speed handlebars.
study.info_and_value: All information is in on-screen text, with no voiceover. It covers venue names (Loft 19, BOLT, Serenity, Grand Central), the BOLT tagline 'Ultimate Sea Coaster' and its 'control how fast your ride goes' feature, and what each zone includes: private cabanas, infinity whirlpool, ocean-front loungers, adults-only status, a private bar, a pool, 360° ocean views, and magic, music and dance shows. There are no prices, booking info or tips; it doesn't say Loft 19 is extra cost. It is saveable as a quick 'what's on the ship' cheat sheet, and the zones map to traveler types, which makes people tag the partner who'd pick each one.
study.pacing: 16 shots in 41.47s, 3.62 cuts per 10s. Median shot is 2.79s, longest 3.54s (the final show shot) and shortest 0.5s (the whirlpool flash at 7.87s). Most shots sit between 2.4 and 3.5s, a steady tour rhythm rather than fast cutting. Each option gets about 10.5s, except the finale at 6.6s. Motion rises within chapters as the camera walks, peaking at 48 at 32s. Sign shots are near-still (3-5.6 for Loft at 3-4s, 7-10 for Serenity at 24.5-25.5s). The video then settles into a calm, nearly static 6.6s finale (motion 2.5-8.9). Cuts mostly do not land on the 0.52s beat grid; only the 28.8s cut is exact.
study.on_screen_text: Hook: two centered lines at about 52% height across the ship's hull. 'CHOOSE YOUR VIBE ON THE' is small and 'CARNIVAL MARDI GRAS' is larger, both in a bold geometric sans, white, uppercase, with a soft drop shadow. It is shown 0-2.47s. Chapters: the venue name in large heavy white uppercase at about 23% height ('LOFT 19', 'BOLT', 'SERENITY', 'GRAND CENTRAL') stays for the whole chapter. Below it a smaller white uppercase subtitle of 2-6 words changes on each cut: 'RETREAT AT SEA', 'GET YOUR OWN PRIVATE CABANA', 'VISIT THE INFINITY WHIRLPOOL', 'RELAX ALONGSIDE THE WAVES', 'ROLLERCOASTER AT SEA', 'CONTROL HOW FAST YOUR RIDE GOES', 'GET SOME 360° OCEAN VIEWS', 'ADULT ONLY RETREAT', 'TAKE SOME TIME AWAY FROM THE KIDS', 'ENJOY A PRIVATE BAR', 'OR RELAX BY THE POOL!', 'ENJOY A SHOW ON THE SHIP!', 'FROM MAGIC TO MUSIC TO DANCING'. All text has a drop shadow and no box, appears and disappears exactly on the cuts, and uses no emoji.
study.audio: Music bed only, no voiceover and no audible natural sound. It is an upbeat track with a pulse of roughly 0.52s (about 115 BPM), with hits at 0.65, 0.91, 1.17, 4.01, 5.56, 6.08, 7.63 and 8.15. A dense run at 9.18-11.25s falls under the ocean-lounger shot, and later hits fall at 13.32-17.46, 22.63-23.15 and 26.77-30.91. Sound and picture are only loosely synced; the cut at 28.8s (onto 'ENJOY A PRIVATE BAR') matches the 28.84 hit, while the other chapter changes fall between beats.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. Chapter changes at 2.47, 12.93, 24.4 and 34.87s are hard cuts onto signage. The 7.87→8.37s cut is a near jump cut within the same whirlpool, and the 16.4→18.13s cut punches from the BOLT car wide into a close-up.
study.effects: No added zooms, graphics, maps or split screens; all movement is camera movement. There is a light-to-moderate saturation and contrast boost, strongest on the BOLT chapter (punchy red, blue and yellow car, crisp pink sunset sky) and the neon Grand Central shots. The pool and whirlpool water reads very cyan. The text has a drop shadow.
study.quality: 1080x1920 at 30fps, h264 at about 15 Mbps, so it is clean and sharp on upload. The footage is phone-shot and handheld but steady, close to gimbal-smooth on the walk-throughs. Exposure is mostly well controlled: the bright hook sky holds cloud detail, and the sunset shots keep both sky color and deck detail. Some overcast Loft 19 and Serenity shots look flat and grey, and the sign shots are slightly soft and noisy. The dream-trip feel comes from the turquoise water, the sunsets and the empty private decks rather than cinematic polish; it reads as an authentic, high-end phone tour.
study.ending: It ends on the busiest, most colorful shot: the live Grand Central performance under purple and pink lights with 'FROM MAGIC TO MUSIC TO DANCING', held 3.54s. There is no on-screen CTA and no final question card. It cuts mid-performance on a static frame, and the night-show ending doesn't match the daytime ship opener, so it doesn't loop seamlessly. The only implied prompt is the opening 'choose your vibe'.
study.why_viral: 1) The 'choose your vibe' frame turns a ship tour into a personal choice. Viewers mentally pick between quiet retreat, thrill coaster, adults-only and nightlife, then comment or tag a partner. 2) Novelty: a rollercoaster, private cabanas and an infinity whirlpool on a ship are 'wait, that's on a cruise?' moments. 3) Strong visual identity: turquoise water, a sunset under coaster track and neon stage lights give the edit a day-to-night arc. 4) A repeatable chapter template (sign, then benefit shots, with a fixed title and changing subtitle) makes it scannable and saveable as a ship cheat sheet.
lessons: Open with the most unusual angle you have on the 'hero' (water-level, low, or framed by foreground) and put the choice question as 2-line text right on the subject, held about 2.5s.
Start each option with a shot of its signage or logo as a free chapter card (2-3.5s, near-static) so viewers instantly know the option changed without needing transitions.
Use a two-tier text system: a big bold venue or option name fixed at about 23% height for the whole chapter, plus a 2-6 word benefit subtitle that changes on every cut.
Give each option a similar slot (about 10-11s, 3-4 shots of 1.5-3.5s) so the comparison feels fair. A 0.5s flash shot inside a chapter adds a jolt without breaking rhythm.
Write subtitles as benefits for a specific traveler ('take some time away from the kids', 'control how fast your ride goes'), not descriptions; that is what drives tags and shares.
Reveal ocean views with a walk-past: start behind a screen, slats or a doorframe and move until the sea opens up, letting the reveal land in the last second of a 3s shot.
Order footage by time of day (bright day, then golden-hour sunset, then neon night) so a list video also feels like a day-to-night story. Put the most colorful, people-filled option last.
Keep empty decks for 'private retreat' options and save visible people for the energy option, so the contrast sells both vibes.

Fix what this edit missed: snap chapter cuts to the beat grid (here about 0.52s), add a closing 'which vibe are you? 1-4' card held about 2s, and add price or 'extra cost' notes so people save it for booking.

name: FULL - Favorite Things on the Norewegian Encore.MOV

study.format: Simple listicle / 'our favorite things' ship tour: a title card over the opening shots, then 4 single-word category labels (SLIDES, SPEEDWAY, POOLS, SHOWS). Each category gets 2-3 clips of about 2.5-4s each. No voiceover; text and music carry it.
study.place: Norwegian Encore, an NCL cruise ship, on a sunny sea day. What makes it special is the top-deck stuff a viewer doesn't expect on a ship: twisting blue water slides and a clear drop-tube tower, a go-kart race track with the ocean behind the barriers, a turquoise pool deck at golden hour, and a Broadway-style pub show (Choir of Man-style set with performers raising pints).
study.audience: People thinking about a cruise, especially families and groups weighing NCL ships. It reads as a traveler or creator sharing personal favorites ('our'), not the cruise line. It makes people save it for ship research, tag the friend who'd race them on the kart track, and comment their own favorite or whether they've sailed Encore.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0-2.6s) is a low handheld angle of the ship's blue-swoosh funnel against a bright sun-flared sky with smoke coming out. A heads-up text block sits mid-screen: 'OUR FAVORITE THINGS ON THE' with a larger 'NORWEGIAN ENCORE' underneath. Music starts with a hit at 0.52s. It stops the scroll because the ship name is right there for anyone who's booked or is considering it. The promise of a ranked set of favorites is answered at 2.6s by a fast pan over a packed pool deck with slides and open ocean (motion 57-68).

beats.what: Low-angle shot of the NCL funnel with the swoosh logo, sun flare, title text 'OUR FAVORITE THINGS ON THE NORWEGIAN ENCORE'
Fast elevated pan across a crowded pool deck: loungers, slides, ocean horizon. Title stays on.
'SLIDES': low-angle pan along the looping blue water slides against a soft, cloudy late-day sky
SLIDES cont.: looking straight up the spiral staircase and clear drop-tube tower, sun flare and lens glints
'SPEEDWAY': handheld drift over the red 'Norwegian Encore Speedway' checkered sign
POV from the driver's seat of a go-kart going around the track's curves, ocean beyond the barriers
Jump cut, then a spectator view of a kart racing past and down the straight under the start lights and the 'ENCORE SPEEDWAY' gantry
'POOLS': slow pan across the turquoise main pool, deck chairs, blue sky
POOLS cont.: backlit golden-hour shot, sun behind the slide tower, sparkling water
'SHOWS': audience-POV of a theater pub show, cast dancing on a bar set with colored stage lights
Closer shot of the finale: performers with a guitar raise pints and point up as stage lights hit them. Video ends mid-moment.

study.choice_format: Not a choice video. It's a 4-item favorites list with no numbers. Each item is labelled with one uppercase word in the same white stroked font at the top-center (~19% from the top). Time per item: SLIDES 5.66s over 2 shots, SPEEDWAY 9.07s over 3 shots (one is a jump cut), POOLS 6.6s over 2 shots, SHOWS ~3.5s+2.5s, about 6s over 2 shots. Items are separated by hard cuts with an instant label swap, no transition. The order builds from daytime sun to golden hour to an indoor night show, so the most emotional, crowd-pleasing moment comes last. There's no explicit ask for comments.
study.action_shots: Go-kart POV 13.93-16.67s (2.7s): a seat-level driver's view moving through the curves at normal speed, motion ~21-27. Spectator/follow shot of a kart 16.67-19.8s (3.1s): handheld from the barrier as a kart passes close and races away, the peak motion of the middle section (45-55 at 17-19s). Pool-deck pan 2.6-5.07s: the fastest camera move in the video (motion 54-68), a whip-like pan across hundreds of guests. Show dancing 26.4-28.93s: a static camera (motion ~3-6) with performers moving. Finale with raised pints 28.93-32.4s, where the crowd-pleasing arm raises arrive along with a dense cluster of audio hits at 30.52-32.07. The action isn't strictly cut to beats; everything plays at real speed.
study.views: Pool deck plus ocean wide at 2.6-5.07s (2.5s), revealed by a fast horizontal pan from the elevated deck. Slides against the sky at 5.07-8.07 (3s), a slow pan/tilt. Looking up the slide tower into the sun at 8.07-10.73 (2.7s), a tilt with a strong flare. Ocean beyond the kart track at 13.93-19.8. Main pool at 19.8-23.93 (4.1s, the longest shot in the video), a slow pan right that reveals the slide tower. The golden-hour backlit pool with the sun behind the slides and glittering water at 23.93-26.4 (2.5s) is the biggest, most cinematic view. It lands at about 75% of the runtime, just before the indoor finale.
study.how_place_is_shown: All handheld phone footage, no drone or gimbal smoothness. Mostly wides and low angles that make the ship's structures feel huge (funnel, slides, tower), with a few mediums (signage, karts, stage). There's no creator in frame; it's all POV/observer. Strangers fill the frame and make it feel alive and busy (crowded deck, kart driver, show cast). The light moves from harsh blue-sky midday, to soft overcast-sunset slides, to warm golden-hour pool, to colorful stage lights at night, which gives a quiet 'full day aboard' arc. The one detail is a red drink cup on the pool ledge at 26s; there's no food or amenity close-up.
study.info_and_value: Light. The ship name (Norwegian Encore) and four named onboard features (water slides, go-kart Speedway, pools, shows), all as on-screen text with no prices, tips or booking info. It's worth saving as a quick visual checklist of what this specific ship has, especially the race track, which is a surprise for many viewers.
study.pacing: 11 shots in 32.4s, 3.09 cuts per 10s, median shot 2.73s, range 2.47-4.13s. That's a very even, relaxed rhythm with no fast montage bursts. The longest hold (4.13s) is the slow pool pan. Fast camera motion opens the video (2.6-5s) and kart action fills the middle (17-19s). The show section starts nearly static (motion ~3 at 26.5-28s) before the finale lifts it. Some cuts sit on audio hits: 2.6 (hit 2.59), 13.93 (13.97), 16.67 (16.55). Others don't line up (5.07, 8.07, 19.8, 28.93), so the cutting is loose rather than beat-locked.
study.on_screen_text: Title 0-5.07s: 'OUR FAVORITE THINGS ON THE' in a smaller line over a larger 'NORWEGIAN ENCORE', centered mid-frame (~40% height). Then labels 'SLIDES' (5.07-10.73), 'SPEEDWAY' (10.73-19.8), 'POOLS' (19.8-26.4) and 'SHOWS' (26.4-end), each positioned top-center at ~19% height. All text is bold, rounded, all-caps sans in white with a thin black outline/shadow, one word at a time, and each label stays on for its whole section. No emoji.
study.audio: Music only (upbeat track), no voiceover or natural sound noticeable. Audio hits come roughly every 1.03s early on (0.52, 1.55, 2.59, 3.62), with a busier cluster at 12.4-15.0 during the Speedway intro and another at 30.5-32.1 under the show finale, so the energy rises as the performers raise their pints. Only a few cuts land on hits (2.6, 13.93, 16.67).
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. Two are effectively jump cuts within the same scene: 16.67 (kart POV continues from almost the same framing) and 23.93 (the pool pan continues, slightly reframed). The label text swaps instantly on the category cuts.
study.effects: No zooms added in post, no graphics. The color looks lightly boosted: saturated blue sky and turquoise water, warm sunset tones. Natural lens flares at 8-10.7s and 24-26s are kept as a feature. No light leaks or freeze frames.
study.quality: 1080x1920, 30fps, HEVC at ~11.2 Mbps, so it's sharp and clean. Footage is clearly handheld phone video with slight shake and some blown-out skies when shooting into the sun. The strong natural color (cobalt sky, teal pools, golden backlight, colored stage lights) does the dream-trip work. Overall it reads as an authentic passenger's phone footage rather than a polished promo, which builds trust.
study.ending: Ends on the show finale: performers raising pints and pointing up under stage spotlights, with a dense cluster of music hits at 30.5-32.07s. It cuts at 32.4s mid-celebration, 3.47s into the last shot, with no CTA or outro. That abrupt cut makes it loop back into the sunny funnel opener.
study.why_viral: The ship name is in the hook, which pulls in a large niche of people who've booked or are considering Norwegian Encore and want to see what's onboard. The surprise feature, a go-kart race track on a cruise ship with a driver's POV, is genuinely shareable and taggable. One-word labels make it instantly scannable and easy to save as a ship checklist. The video moves from midday to golden hour to an evening show and ends on a feel-good, arms-up finale.
lessons: Put the exact ship, resort or destination name in the first frame as a two-line title, with the name on the second line set larger than the setup words.
Follow a static or slow opener within 2.5-3s with your busiest, fastest-moving wide (a crowded deck pan, a pool reveal) to prove the promise right away.
Label each list item with one ALL-CAPS word in white bold with a thin black stroke, placed top-center around 18-20% from the top, and keep it on for the whole section.
Give each item 2 shots of 2.5-4s (about 5.5-9s per item). Use one establishing or low-angle wide, then one action or POV shot of someone actually using it.
Feature the most unexpected amenity (go-karts on a ship, a glass-floor bridge, etc.) as a POV ride shot. It's the clip people tag friends on.
Order items by time of day (midday, golden hour, night lights) so a simple list feels like a full day, and save the warm sunset backlight for the second-to-last item.
End on a human, celebratory moment (a crowd cheering, performers raising glasses) timed under the busiest part of the music, then cut abruptly at about 3.5s into the shot so it loops.
Keep natural lens flares and shoot slides or towers from low angles into the sun. It makes phone footage look epic without any effects.

study.format: Cruise ship 'spend a day with us' tour, built as a voiceover-driven checklist. One continuous narration names a venue every 2–4 seconds, and each name gets a 1.3–4.5s clip of that venue (sign, then space, then the creator using it). The order runs from day to night: a slide POV hook, then pools, outdoor deck games, indoor games, views and food, photo spots, evening entertainment, and a cocktail plus the glass ocean walk at night. It is a hybrid of day-in-the-life and amenity tour, with no numbering or ranking.
study.place: Norwegian Cruise Line's new ship Norwegian Luna, an ocean cruise filmed in port and at sea under bright Caribbean sun with turquoise water. What makes it look special is the novelty hardware: the Aqua Slide Coaster with lit, colored tubes, an infinity-edge pool against the open ocean, and neon-lit indoor game zones ('The Stadium', Glow Court with a projected underwater basketball floor). It also shows the Moon Climber rope course, Tea Time Mini Golf, the Luna Midway arcade with interactive dartboards, the Dry Drop Slide capsule, the Indulge Food Hall, sculptural white wave lounges, a chrome crescent-moon photo spot, the Improv comedy club, a live band at Sid Norman's Pourhouse, tablet-ordered cocktails, and a glass-floored walkway over the wake at night.
study.audience: Cruisers who are considering or already booked on the new Luna, plus families and couples who like activity-heavy ships. It works as a save-for-later planning list ('what to do on board') and gets shared with the travel partner ('we have to do the slide'). It reads as a travel-creator couple ('with us', 'we loved'), possibly partnered with NCL given the branded cup close-up. It is not an official ad, but it is very brand-friendly.
study.hook: Frame 1 is a POV from inside an NCL-branded blue tube raft, perched at the top of the Aqua Slide Coaster against a deep blue sky with one white cloud. The voiceover starts immediately at 0.08s: 'Spend a day with us on the Norwegian Luna.' A centered white two-line title repeats that line. Within 1.43s it cuts to the inside of the tube rushing past glowing yellow portholes, and the motion graph jumps to 42–50. It stops the scroll because a first-person slide drop gives instant motion and a stomach-drop feeling. The ship name and the 'day with us' promise land in the first 2 seconds, telling viewers this is a full tour.

beats.what: POV in the raft at the top of the Aqua Slide Coaster, blue sky; title 'Spend a day with us on the Norwegian Luna'
Inside the slide tube: green tunnel with glowing portholes, then red/cyan translucent sections rushing past, with a clear-tube exit at the end; VO 'The Aqua Slide Coaster is a must-do'
Hand holds an NCL-branded frozen drink with lime, out-of-focus pool deck behind, then the focus shifts to the pool and the big 'LUNA' screen
Creator from behind in the infinity pool, turquoise water meeting the ocean horizon; VO 'Infinity Beach pools are my favorite'
Horizon Park sign, then a pan to loungers on green turf with port and sea view, creator walking through
Cornhole boards on turf with the funnel and waterslides behind; VO 'play games in the sun'
Neon 'THE STADIUM' sign

Looking up at the rope course structure, then Tea Time Mini Golf holes under the waterslides
